A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Time-To-Inconsistency study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E support reliable comparison; the extra page in v3 results from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original survival-model analyses of 36,951 conversational turns, including held-out prediction results, risk monitoring, and proportional-hazards diagnostics.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses and their results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The semantic-drift features, Cox/AFT/RSF formulations, interaction terms, and conditional-failure monitoring procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MT-Consistency with the same 700 questions, 39 subjects, seven domain clusters, four difficulty bands, and eight adversarial prompt types. Appendices B-C retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain the same Cox, AFT, and Random Survival Forest comparisons. Table 4 retains the same AFT monitor and drift-threshold baseline.

E3.justification: The nine evaluated LLMs, eight-turn horizon, filtering, stratified 80/20 split, five-fold training-pool cross-validation, evaluation metrics, and monitoring protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: The Cox-versus-AFT feature-importance check in Figure 1, risk-stratification analysis, retrospective monitoring analysis, and Appendix D diagnostics are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same conversation-level cluster-robust standard errors, log-rank tests, and Schoenfeld-residual tests. Neither adds seed counts, repeated-run information, or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 1 and the result entries in Tables 1-4 and 7 are unchanged. Examples include Weibull AFT's C-index of 0.874, Weibull AFT with interactions' IBS of 0.175, and the monitor alerting 76% of failing conversations.

T1.justification: The event, survival, hazard, and drift definitions and model equations are identical. Appendix A retains the same Weibull, log-normal, and log-logistic survival and hazard formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about survival-based evaluation, abrupt versus cumulative drift, AFT performance, and early-warning monitoring.

C2.justification: Interpretations of drift, adaptation, and proportional-hazards violations are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning benchmark scope, eight-turn conversations, binary failures, one embedding model, and retrospective monitoring.

D1.justification: Feature-construction details, prompt templates, and Appendix E's hyperparameter grids and selected values are unchanged. The updated evaluation-harness URL is part of a background reference, not a new code or data disclosure for this study.

R1.justification: Matching references by work identity reveals no added or removed works or changed research positioning. MultiChallenge's switch from Sirdeshmukh et al. to Deshpande et al., and other author/year/venue revisions, are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Acknowledgments section disclosing fellowship and research funding and updates citation labels and bibliographic metadata. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Acknowledgments change page 11's layout, and expanded references spill onto a third bibliography page, shifting the appendices. Table 5 replaces underscores in computer_security and truthful_qa with spaces; Figure 1 and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds funding transparency and fuller author and publication details for existing references, modestly improving attribution and source traceability. These documentation gains are limited: the scientific methods, empirical support, and limitations are unchanged.
